instruction_covers: GeoDataFrame.set_crs must keep an existing spatial_partitions geometry instead of dropping it to None
When spatial_partitions is None it stays None, and set_crs still sets the frame CRS
The copy() fix is the stated analogue
label: broken
notes: Repo verified: _Frame.set_crs (core.py:154) returns map_partitions without propagating partitions; copy() (core.py:171) only does spatial_partitions.copy() with no CRS update; calculate_spatial_partitions (core.py:115) builds a GeoSeries whose CRS is None. The minimal instruction-faithful fix (reattach/propagate partitions per the copy analogue) keeps geometries but leaves partitions CRS None and fails both CRS assertions, so the tie-break minimal-fix test gives not_inferable. GeoSeries shares the single _Frame.set_crs so preservation propagates mechanically, but the CRS assignment is new semantics beyond the stated analogue.

unstated.what: set_crs must assign the new CRS onto the preserved spatial_partitions, not merely reattach them: after set_crs('EPSG:4326') spatial_partitions.crs must equal the new CRS, even though calculate_spatial_partitions builds partitions with CRS None and the copy() analogue only does spatial_partitions.copy()

GeoSeries.set_crs must preserve spatial partitions and set their CRS too, although the instruction and example name only GeoDataFrame.set_crs; set_crs is defined once on _Frame so the same fix applies, but the CRS assignment still fails the minimal-fix test
